# dlasv2

> Computes the singular value decomposition of a 2-by-2 triangular matrix.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dlasv2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasv2';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dlasv2( f, g, h, ssmin, ssmax, snr, csr, snl, csl ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | The (1,1) element |
| `g` | `number` | The (1,2) element |
| `h` | `number` | The (2,2) element |
| `ssmin` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): abs(SSMIN) is the smaller singular value |
| `ssmax` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): abs(SSMAX) is the larger singular value |
| `snr` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `snr` |
| `csr` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CSR, SNR) is a unit right singular vector for the singular value abs(SSMAX) |
| `snl` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `snl` |
| `csl` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CSL, SNL) is a unit left singular vector for the singular value abs(SSMAX) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `f`: The (1,1) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `g`: The (1,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `h`: The (2,2) element of the 2-by-2 matrix.
- `ssmin`: abs(`SSMIN`) is the smaller singular value.
- `ssmax`: abs(`SSMAX`) is the larger singular value.
- `csr`: The vector (`CSR`, `SNR`) is a unit right singular vector for the singular value abs(`SSMAX`).
- `csl`: The vector (`CSL`, `SNL`) is a unit left singular vector for the singular value abs(`SSMAX`).

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dlasv2.strided( f, g, h, ssmin, ssmax, snr, csr, snl, csl ) → void
```

Computes the singular value decomposition of a 2-by-2 triangular matrix, using alternative indexing semantics.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `f` | `number` | The (1,1) element |
| `g` | `number` | The (1,2) element |
| `h` | `number` | The (2,2) element |

| `ssmax` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): abs(SSMAX) is the larger singular value |

| `csr` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CSR, SNR) is a unit right singular vector for the singular value abs(SSMAX) |
| `snl` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): `snl` |
| `csl` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Output (length-1 array): the vector (CSL, SNL) is a unit left singular vector for the singular value abs(SSMAX) |

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dlasv2()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DLASV2`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dlasv2.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import dlasv2 from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/dlasv2';

// Using the standard interface:
const ssmin = new Float64Array( 1 );
const ssmax = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const csr = new Float64Array( 1 );
const snl = new Float64Array( 1 );
const csl = new Float64Array( 1 );

dlasv2( 1, 1, 1, ssmin, ssmax, snr, csr, snl, csl );
let out = {
	'ssmin': ssmin[ 0 ],
	'ssmax': ssmax[ 0 ],
	'snr': snr[ 0 ],
	'csr': csr[ 0 ],
	'snl': snl[ 0 ],
	'csl': csl[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );

// Using the strided interface:
dlasv2.strided( 1, 1, 1, ssmin, ssmax, snr, csr, snl, csl );
out = {
	'ssmin': ssmin[ 0 ],
	'ssmax': ssmax[ 0 ],
	'snr': snr[ 0 ],
	'csr': csr[ 0 ],
	'snl': snl[ 0 ],
	'csl': csl[ 0 ]
};
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DLASV2`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DLASV2 computes the singular value decomposition of a 2-by-2 triangular matrix

$$
\begin{bmatrix} F & G \\ 0 & H \end{bmatrix}
$$

On return, abs(`SSMAX`) is the larger singular value, abs(`SSMIN`) is the smaller singular value, and (`CSL`,`SNL`) and (`CSR`,`SNR`) are the left and right singular vectors for abs(`SSMAX`), giving the decomposition

$$
\begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSL} & \mathrm{SNL} \\ -\mathrm{SNL} & \mathrm{CSL} \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} F & G \\ 0 & H \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{CSR} & -\mathrm{SNR} \\ \mathrm{SNR} & \mathrm{CSR} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathrm{SSMAX} & 0 \\ 0 & \mathrm{SSMIN} \end{bmatrix}
$$

### Further Details

Any input parameter may be aliased with any output parameter.

Barring over/underflow and assuming a guard digit in subtraction, all output quantities are correct to within a few units in the last place (ulps).

In IEEE arithmetic, the code works correctly if one matrix element is infinite.

Overflow will not occur unless the largest singular value itself overflows or is within a few ulps of overflow.

Underflow is harmless if underflow is gradual. Otherwise, results may correspond to a matrix modified by perturbations of size near the underflow threshold.

</section>
